data.command: How do attackers achieve execution via scheduled tasks T1053.005?

data.text:
T1053.005 — Scheduled Task/Job: Scheduled Task (Windows). Attackers abuse the Windows Task Scheduler to get code to run on a schedule or at a trigger, gaining execution, persistence, and often privilege escalation. Common mechanics:

Command-line creation
- schtasks.exe /create /tn "\Microsoft\Windows\Updater" /tr "C:\Users\Public\svc.dll,Update" /sc onlogon /ru SYSTEM /f
- /sc supports MINUTE, HOURLY, DAILY, ONLOGON, ONSTART, ONIDLE, ONEVENT, ONCE.
- Task runs as the creator by default, or /ru SYSTEM /ru "NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM" for higher rights (requires privileges).
- /tr accepts any executable; a full command line, a script host (rundll32, mshta, powershell -enc <base64>), or a bare path.

COM / API creation (stealthier, avoids schtasks.exe on the command line)
- ITaskService -> ITaskDefinition -> RegisterTaskDefinition via PowerShell, C#, VBScript, or Office macros.
- Action type TASK_ACTION_EXEC with ExecAction Path/Arguments; also TASK_ACTION_COM_HANDLER for COM hijack-style execution.
- Setting the task's author to a Microsoft-sounding string makes it blend into \Microsoft\Windows\ subtrees.

Trigger abuse for immediate execution
- ONLOGON / ONSTART / ONIDLE / ONEVENT (WMI or event-log based) fire without waiting for a clock time.
- Modifying an existing legitimate task (e.g. appending an action) reuses trusted task names.
- Daily/weekly triggers with a past StartBoundary can cause an immediate catch-up run.

Consistency and defense evasion
- Tasks created via the API are harder to spot in process telemetry than schtasks.exe, but both land on disk in C:\Windows\System32\Tasks\ and in the registry under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Schedule\TaskCache\.
- Store tasks at a non-standard path or revoke read access so non-admins can't enumerate them.
- Use a hidden task (Settings.Hidden = true) to conceal it from the Task Scheduler UI.
- Point the action at copy in a user-writable path (TEMP, Public, AppData) or a LOLBin to reduce footprint.

Watch for (detections)
- Process creation: schtasks.exe with /create, especially /ru SYSTEM or /ru "NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM".
- rundll32/mshta/powershell/wscript launched with an unusual parent of svchost.exe (Task Scheduler).
- New or modified files under C:\Windows\System32\Tasks\.
- Registry writes to ...\Schedule\TaskCache\Tree\ for task names not part of the OS baseline.

Cross-platform note: the sibling technique T1053.003 covers the same idea on Linux/macOS via cron (/etc/crontab, /etc/cron.*, crontab -e, and @reboot entries), which is what an equivalent on this box would look like.
